title: client-transition-playbook-retries-streaming-and-changelog-automation
text:
client-transition-playbook-retries-streaming-and-changelog-automation

description:
Produce a cross-language transition playbook for SDK users migrating from v1 -> v2. Deliverables include: a migration guide with concrete code examples (Python, TypeScript, Go), an ergonomic section for streaming APIs and retry semantics, a deprecation schedule for removed v1 surface area, and an automated changelog pipeline that synthesizes commits/PRs into user-facing migration notes. This ticket coordinates docs, small shim packages, and a codemod prototype for common call patterns.

acceptance_criteria:
A consolidated migration guide page exists with side-by-side v1->v2 examples for Python/TS/Go
Streaming ergonomics documented: pattern for incremental consumption, cancellation, and backpressure in each language
Retry semantics table published and a recommended client configuration for low-latency vs high-throughput workloads
Changelog automation pipeline implemented in CI that produces a draft CHANGELOG.md and categorized migration notes from merged PRs
Codemod prototype (Python) that rewrites common blocking streaming patterns to the new async iterator pattern
Documentation reviewed and signed off by Docs, SDK, and Developer Experience teams

updates:
2025-02-10: Ticket created after SDK working group triage. Scoped to docs + automation + small tooling (codemod).
2025-02-14: Architecture sync — agreed to standardize on an async iterator style for streaming in Python/TS and a channel-based API for Go. Noted backward compatibility options: compat-shim for TS and Python, explicit deprecation warnings for Go users.
2025-02-18: Prototype codemod initial commit (python) rewrites synchronous .stream() loops to async for constructs. Performance and safety review needed.
2025-02-21: Docs draft uploaded to /sdk/migration/v1-to-v2. Requesting review from Docs (Sofia Ramos) and DX (Liam O'Connor).
2025-02-25: Decided on changelog automation approach: parse PR titles with Conventional Commits + label mapping to produce 'Migration Notes' and 'Deprecated APIs' sections. CI job will open a draft release PR for maintainers to edit.
2025-02-28: Design review complete. Added example patterns for retry-with-idempotency-key and streaming cancellation tokens across languages. Next: finalize codemod tests and CI pipeline steps.
2025-03-01: Began writing release checklist and deprecation schedule. Coordinating with Support to prepare canned migration responses.

notes:
Trade-off: aggressive compat shims increase complexity and maintenance; chosen approach is to provide lightweight shims for TS/Python but require explicit migration for Go to keep API surface idiomatic.
Open question: whether to include automated opt-in migration via a CLI flag in the shim. Security team flagged potential behavior changes for audit-heavy customers.
Follow-up: add telemetry events for deprecated API usage to inform migration friction metrics.
